text:
IncidentBot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate detected for private VPC egress to internet (customer=lumina, env=prod). 504/502 spike starting ~2191234558, p50 latency up 3x. Paging oncall Alex. Details: https://metrics/redwood/alerts/2191234567 :rotating_light:

Alex: I'm on it. seeing 504s spiking from inference-gateway -> egress-nat (10.3.8.0/24). Is this across all AZs?

Jordan: quick look at the logs: a lot of `connection reset by peer` and `upstream timed out (110)` on gw-proxy. Conntrack count on the NAT host is near max (430k/450k). Could be ephemeral port exhaustion.

Lee: jumping in — I see a peering flap between vpc-lumina and core-transit in eu-west-1 around 2191234500 that correlates. Route table failover appears to have created asymmetric return paths to the NAT gateway, causing sessions to be dropped.

Alex: timeline makes sense. customer requests are hitting gw and SNAT state doesn't match return path. Is there a short mitigation we can do to restore connectivity quickly?

Lee: short term: add a temporary route in lumina RT to prefer the healthy transit appliance (10.10.4.0/24) and increase conntrack on the NAT host. Steps: 1) ssh to nat-prod-3 2) sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=800000 3) echo 1536 65535 > /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range

Jordan: doing conntrack bump now on nat-prod-3, doing graceful sync across NAT pool. Also clearing old conntrack entries for 10.3.8.0/24: 
```
# careful; this removes state for in-flight requests
sudo conntrack -D -s 10.3.8.0/24
```

Maria: I can push the temporary route change for the customer's VPC. Is there any risk to breaking existing flows?

Lee: minimal if we restrict to the single prefix used for inference egress. I'll stage the route change in the playground RT first then apply. Will post route change commands.

Annika: Customer impact: Lumina reported increased failed inferences, some timeouts on scheduled jobs. Estimated affected percentage ~12% of traffic in the last 10m. CS is drafting a status to send to Lumina once we have mitigation confirmed.

Alex: After conntrack bump + port range change I still see a tail of 504s but p95 falling. Good. Maria, when you apply the route change can you confirm the gateway path (traceroute) so we know return path is via the same transit appliance?

Maria: Route change applied to rt-lumina-euwest (will prefer 10.10.4.0/24). Traceroute from gw-proxy now shows symmetric path through transit-4.

Jordan: Confirming metrics: 5xx rate dropping from 18% -> 2% within 3 minutes of route change. Conntrack freed 120k entries after the change. Still seeing intermittent resets for a few long-lived streams.

Alex: Good. I'll keep monitoring for 15m then hand to NetOps for full root-cause. EngInfraBot, please create an incident ticket and assign to NetOps for follow-up and PM/CS communication.

EngInfraBot: Created INC-2026-219123 (priority P1) -> assigned to Lee (NetOps). Postmortem owner: Jordan. Notifying infra@ and cs@.

Lee: Root-cause hypothesis: peering BGP session briefly converged causing asymmetric SNAT. Follow-ups: 1) audit peering route propagation and BGP timers, 2) add health-based route preference to avoid failover to broken appliance, 3) increase default ephemeral port range and conntrack headroom for NAT fleet, 4) plan NAT pool horizontal scale and add monitoring for conntrack headroom alerts.

Annika: CS update ready to send — brief explanation + mitigation + ETA for root-cause analysis. Waiting for Alex to confirm we can mark incident as "mitigated".

Alex: Marking mitigated at 2191234599. Customer impact resolved to acceptable level; handing post-incident to NetOps and Eng for RCA. Will schedule follow-up postmortem and action items. :white_check_mark:

Lee: Taking ownership. Will coordinate with network provider to get BGP session logs and check transit appliance health. Will also file change request for NAT pool sizing and ephemeral port defaults.

Jordan: I'll capture metric dashboards and add a regression test for asymmetric-route->SNAT-failures to the incident playbook.

Maria: Notifying Lumina with the drafted message and offering a bridge if they want realtime updates.

Annika: Lumina acknowledged and appreciates the quick mitigation.

Alex: Thanks team. Postmortem ETA: 72 hours. Filing follow-ups in INC-2026-219123. Closing slack thread for active paging; please update INC ticket with any new findings. :handshake:
